authorship.assistanceDisclosure: Human-directed request; model-assisted research synthesis, original synthetic fixture authorship, implementation, and prefreeze verification. Independent review and release authorization remain separate recorded events.

artifact.title: KINGDOM Aesthetic Plurality & Making Relations Atlas — Phase 0

constitutionalBoundaries.opening: A form can be measured without being beautiful. A synthetic attributed response can be recorded without becoming universal. A work can be made without settling who authored, owns, may publish, or should adopt it. This atlas keeps those seams open so creation remains plural.

assumptions: A finite representation x and a finite declared transformation set G are supplied.
nonclaims: The stabilizer size is not an aesthetic scalar and does not imply preference.
equationCards.notation: Stab_G(x) = { g in G | g·x = x }
equationCards.title: Symmetry is invariance under declared transformations

assumptions: The fixture uses dyadic rational probabilities so verification remains exact.
nonclaims: Entropy is not meaning, quality, beauty, or cultural significance.
equationCards.title: Entropy depends on a declared distribution

assumptions: Every code and specimen is explicitly finite.
nonclaims: A shorter declared encoding is not a better work or a universal simplicity fact.
equationCards.title: Description length depends on code and model

assumptions: The representation and finite reference set are named.
nonclaims: Reference-relative absence is not global originality, priority, authorship, or value.
equationCards.notation: N_R(x) = 1 when repr(x) is not in R; otherwise 0
equationCards.title: Novelty is relative to a reference and representation

assumptions: All fixture coordinates belong only to an invented decision-vector register and are declared as maximize directions.
nonclaims: The frontier supplies no artifact evaluation, aesthetic judgment, winner, scalar order, or recommendation.
equationCards.notation: x is dominated when some y is >= on all declared objectives and > on at least one
equationCards.title: Non-domination preserves plural abstract coordinates

nonclaims: Majority relations do not become a coherent collective taste or aesthetic authority.
equationCards.notation: A ≻ B, B ≻ C, C ≻ A
equationCards.title: Pairwise aggregation can cycle

nonclaims: Lineage does not settle intention, authorship, ownership, permission, or endorsement.
equationCards.notation: ancestor(u,v) iff a directed path u -> ... -> v exists

nonclaims: Probability and occurrence do not establish intention, authorship, ownership, or permission.

equationCards.title: Occurrence under a distribution is not intention

assumptions: A finite feasible set, directed transition set, and start state are declared.

equationCards.title: Feasibility and reachability are different sets

nonEquivalences.reason: Invariance is computed from a declared representation and transformations; an aesthetic judgment is an attributed evaluative act.
Distributional uncertainty does not encode semantic, historical, cultural, or evaluative significance.
The fixture reverses the ordering under a second declared code.
The same representation is absent from one reference and present in another.
Multiple invented coordinate vectors can remain on a frontier without any artifact relation, scalarization, or choice rule.
Pairwise majorities can be cyclic even when each synthetic ballot is transitive.
A derivation edge records ancestry only.
A supported observed outcome supplies no maker statement or legal conclusion.
A feasible state can be disconnected from the declared start under the declared transitions.
A path in a model does not record a voluntary adoption event.
A reported encounter and an explicit evaluation are separate attributed acts.
The atlas records who judged what under which terms; it grants no metaphysical or moral conversion.
Attribution establishes that a statement is in the fixture, not that it exhausts interpretation or proves an inner state.
Context records are partial and attributed; they do not define a people or settle rights.
A selection event is scoped to one institution and procedure.
Availability, rights terms, and voluntary reuse are separately recorded relations.
One scoped reuse event need not affirm every statement, interpretation, or future use.
Consequences can inform repair without becoming a retroactive universal verdict.
A scoped technical access condition is important but does not settle aesthetic judgment or every user need.
A typed translation edge can name unresolved or lost distinctions and therefore is not an identity edge.
A translation or derivation record does not settle authorization or rights.

sourceBindings.bindingRole: Information entropy orientation for one exact dyadic fixture.
sourceBindings.citation: Claude E. Shannon, A Mathematical Theory of Communication, Bell System Technical Journal 27(3), 379–423 (1948).

sourceBindings.bindingRole: Description-length orientation; the atlas emphasizes declared-code dependence.
sourceBindings.citation: Jorma Rissanen, Modeling by shortest data description, Automatica 14(5), 465–471 (1978).

sourceBindings.bindingRole: Algorithmic-description orientation with explicit reference-model dependence.
sourceBindings.citation: A. N. Kolmogorov, Three approaches to the quantitative definition of information, Problems of Information Transmission 1(1), 3–11 (1965); English edition 1968.

sourceBindings.bindingRole: Historical orientation for cyclic pairwise aggregation.
sourceBindings.citation: Nicolas de Condorcet, Essai sur l’application de l’analyse à la probabilité des décisions rendues à la pluralité des voix, Imprimerie Royale (1785).

sourceBindings.bindingRole: Social-choice orientation for limits of preference aggregation; no governance procedure is imported.
sourceBindings.citation: Kenneth J. Arrow, Social Choice and Individual Values, Cowles Commission Monograph 12 (1951).

sourceBindings.bindingRole: One attributed processing-fluency model, preserved as a proposal rather than a universal law.
sourceBindings.citation: Rolf Reber, Norbert Schwarz, and Piotr Winkielman, Processing Fluency and Aesthetic Pleasure: Is Beauty in the Perceiver’s Processing Experience?, Personality and Social Psychology Review 8(4), 364–382 (2004).

sourceBindings.bindingRole: Empirical counterweight to universal conversion from symmetry to aesthetic judgment.
sourceBindings.citation: Helmut Leder, Pablo P. L. Tinio, David Brieber, Tonio Kröner, Thomas Jacobsen, and Raphael Rosenberg, Symmetry Is Not a Universal Law of Beauty, Empirical Studies of the Arts 37(1), 104–114 (2019).

sourceBindings.bindingRole: Individual disagreement orientation limited to abstract randomized patterns.
sourceBindings.citation: Jay Friedenberg, Beauty in the Eye of the Beholder: Individual Differences in Preference for Randomized Visual Patterns, Experimental Psychology 66(2), 123–136 (2019).

sourceBindings.bindingRole: Cross-cultural empirical orientation preserving both commonality and difference without culture scores.
sourceBindings.citation: Eline Van Geert, Rong Ding, and Johan Wagemans, A Cross-Cultural Comparison of Aesthetic Preferences for Neatly Organized Compositions: Native Chinese- Versus Native Dutch-Speaking Samples, Empirical Studies of the Arts 43(1), 250–275 (2025; online 2024).

sourceBindings.bindingRole: Official cultural-expression diversity context; no compliance or legal conclusion.
sourceBindings.citation: UNESCO, Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions, adopted 20 October 2005.

sourceBindings.bindingRole: Boundary context against treating cultural expressions as ownerless fixture material.
sourceBindings.citation: World Intellectual Property Organization, Traditional Cultural Expressions, official topic page.

sourceBindings.bindingRole: Official Indigenous-rights context; no culture is represented by a synthetic fixture.
sourceBindings.citation: United Nations General Assembly, United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, A/RES/61/295 (2007), especially Article 31.

sourceBindings.bindingRole: Technical access orientation kept distinct from aesthetic judgment; no conformance claim.
sourceBindings.citation: W3C Accessibility Guidelines Working Group, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, W3C Recommendation 12 December 2024.

sourceBindings.bindingRole: Jurisdiction-specific legal context for keeping stochastic generation, human contribution, and authorship questions distinct; no legal advice or conclusion.
sourceBindings.citation: U.S. Copyright Office, Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 2: Copyrightability (January 2025).

nonclaims: Four preserving transforms do not make the pattern beautiful, good, important, finished, or preferred.
premises: The four positions are a declared 2-by-2 representation.
A transform acts by the listed permutation and no unlisted transform is inferred.
syntheticFixtures.title: One finite pattern has four preserving transformations in the declared set

nonclaims: Three halves of a bit says nothing about meaning, response, aesthetic judgment, culture, or worth.
premises: Counts are positive integers and total four.
Logarithms use base two.
syntheticFixtures.title: Exact entropy for a declared three-symbol distribution

nonclaims: Neither encoding is an aesthetic judgment, quality metric, or universal complexity measure.
premises: Only literal symbol lengths are summed.
Each declared code is a fixture convention, not a claim of optimal compression.
syntheticFixtures.title: Two declared codes reverse the description-length ordering

nonclaims: Absence from REFERENCE_ALPHA does not establish global originality, priority, authorship, ownership, or aesthetic worth.
premises: Representation is exact string identity in this fixture.
Reference sets are finite and explicitly named.
syntheticFixtures.title: The same representation is absent from one reference and present in another

nonclaims: The vectors are not artifacts or judgments; the frontier ranks, selects, and recommends nothing.
premises: Both integer coordinates are declared as maximize directions.
No weights, scalarization, or choice rule exists.
syntheticFixtures.title: Three invented vectors remain on a Pareto frontier under two declared coordinates

nonclaims: The fixture produces no ranking; the cycle authorizes no tie-breaker, institution, winner, consensus, recommendation, or collective aesthetic voice.
premises: A, B, and C are opaque synthetic symbols, not artifacts, people, cultures, or aesthetic judgments.
Each fixed ballot is a strict order over the same symbols and every ballot has equal count one.
syntheticFixtures.title: Three fixed orders over opaque synthetic symbols yield a cyclic pairwise relation

nonclaims: The graph records no intention, authorship, ownership, permission, licence, endorsement, or creative-credit allocation; translation is not identity or guaranteed meaning preservation.
premises: Nodes and derivation edges are complete for this fixture only.
Edges point from predecessor to derived version.
syntheticFixtures.title: A finite derivation graph records lineage and nothing more

nonclaims: The distribution and occurrence settle no intention, authorship, ownership, copyrightability, permission, or adoption question.
premises: The three rational probabilities sum exactly to one.
The fixture performs no sampling and uses no randomness.
syntheticFixtures.title: A supported observed outcome does not establish intention or authorship

nonclaims: Model reachability is not real-world capability, permission, publication, adoption, or aesthetic merit.
premises: All four states are feasible by declaration.
Only listed directed transitions are available.
syntheticFixtures.title: One feasible state is unreachable from the declared start

nonclaims: Neither synthetic label is a truth verdict, person trait, culture trait, winner, or recommendation.
premises: Both roles and the encountered form are synthetic.
No participant or population inference is permitted.
syntheticFixtures.title: Two synthetic attributed judgments disagree without collapse

nonclaims: The response token is not an aesthetic judgment, population estimate, person trait, or universal response.
premises: The role, form, context, and response token are synthetic.
A response report is not silently retyped as an evaluative judgment.
syntheticFixtures.title: A synthetic attributed response is recorded without an aesthetic judgment

nonclaims: Recording the sentence does not prove an inner state, exhaust interpretation, assign authorship, or establish ownership.
premises: The form, event, role, and statement are synthetic.
The statement is recorded exactly as fixture data.
syntheticFixtures.title: A maker statement remains attributed without settling meaning

contexts.description: Encountered as a repeated workshop exercise.
Encountered as an isolated archive fragment.

nonclaims: The invented contexts do not model, score, summarize, or stand in for any culture or living tradition.
premises: Both contexts are invented analytic placeholders and represent no real community or tradition.
No contextual description implies permission or ownership.
syntheticFixtures.title: The same abstract form is situated in two invented fixture contexts

nonclaims: Selection supplies no global rank, universal judgment, recommendation, adoption, or truth status.
premises: The institution, procedure, form, and event are synthetic.
The fixture records selection, not why every selector acted.
syntheticFixtures.title: One synthetic selection event stays scoped to its declared procedure

nonclaims: Availability does not create permission, licence, reuse, endorsement, or adoption.
premises: The route, publisher, artifact, and rights label are synthetic placeholders.
No actual publication or rights grant occurs.
syntheticFixtures.title: A synthetic publication event occurs without an adoption event

nonclaims: One use does not endorse every interpretation, future use, publisher, maker statement, or institution.
premises: The adopter, artifact, and use context are synthetic.
The adoption record contains no endorsement statement.
syntheticFixtures.title: A scoped synthetic adoption does not imply endorsement

nonclaims: Wear and repair do not prove success, failure, aesthetic truth, deserved reward, or deserved punishment.
premises: The artifact and maintenance events are synthetic.
A repair can be recorded without assigning reward or punishment.
syntheticFixtures.title: A synthetic repair event records aftermath without retroactive verdict

nonclaims: Two synthetic checks establish neither aesthetic quality nor conformance, universal access, completion, or recommendation.
premises: The content and checklist are synthetic.
The checklist is not a WCAG conformance evaluation.
syntheticFixtures.title: A scoped technical access check remains separate from aesthetic judgment

lanes.definition: A declared arrangement, pattern, specification, or material configuration described without an aesthetic verdict.
lanes.label: Form

lanes.definition: A bounded transformation, assembly, selection, or revision event with declared inputs and outputs.
lanes.label: Making event

lanes.definition: An attributed statement about a making event, purpose, process, or form; it records the statement rather than proving an inner state or exclusive meaning.
lanes.label: Maker statement

lanes.definition: A situated report of an encounter, attributed in Phase 0 only to an explicitly synthetic role and never generalized to a person or population.
lanes.label: Attributed response

lanes.definition: An attributed evaluation under a declared vocabulary, method, date, and context, preserved alongside possible disagreement.
lanes.label: Aesthetic judgment

lanes.definition: A declared historical, social, material, ritual, or interpretive context represented without reducing a culture or community to an essence.
lanes.label: Context and tradition

lanes.definition: A documented acceptance, exhibition, acquisition, commissioning, curriculum, or award event under a stated institutional procedure.
lanes.label: Institutional selection

lanes.definition: A documented act of making an artifact available at a declared location and under declared terms.
lanes.label: Publication

lanes.definition: A distinct, voluntary, context-bound choice to reuse, perform, integrate, maintain, or carry a form.
lanes.label: Adoption

lanes.definition: Observed consequences, maintenance, contestation, repair, withdrawal, succession, or retirement after a making, publication, or adoption event.
lanes.label: Aftermath

mathematicalRegisters.definition: A finite register of invented integer coordinate vectors used only to demonstrate multiobjective non-domination.
A finite register of fixed strict orders over opaque invented symbols used only to demonstrate a pairwise aggregation cycle.

relationTypes.definition: A bounded description refers to a declared form or event.
A declared form is an output of a declared making event.
An attributed statement concerns a declared form or event.
An attributed synthetic response concerns one declared encounter.
An attributed aesthetic judgment evaluates one declared object under named terms.
A statement, response, judgment, or event is bounded to a declared context.
An artifact was selected through a declared institutional procedure.
An artifact was made available through a declared publication event.
An artifact was voluntarily reused in one declared adoption context.
A declared event has a later recorded consequence or stewardship event.
A version has a declared lineage edge from another version.
A form or making event is bounded by a declared feasibility, access, material, or rights condition.
Two attributed judgments differ without forced resolution.
A typed boundary says one relation must not be silently converted into another.
A version is declared as a translation with named source and target languages, explicit possible meaning loss, and separately unresolved rights.

terms.definition: The subset of declared transformations under which a declared finite representation remains invariant.
nonclaims: Not a universal property independent of representation or transform set.
Not an aesthetic judgment.

terms.definition: Expected information under a declared finite probability distribution and logarithm base.
nonclaims: Not semantic meaning.
Not aesthetic value.

terms.definition: A bit length under a named code or model-description convention.
nonclaims: Not code-independent complexity.
Not quality or worth.

terms.definition: Absence of a declared representation from a named finite reference set.
nonclaims: Not global originality.
Not priority, authorship, or ownership.

terms.definition: No declared alternative is at least as strong on every declared objective and strictly stronger on at least one.
nonclaims: Not a scalar ordering.
Not a preferred choice or recommendation.

terms.definition: A relation computed from declared finite preference orders by pairwise counts.
nonclaims: Need not be transitive.
Not a coherent collective taste or authority.

terms.definition: A finite directed acyclic graph whose edges declare version derivation.
nonclaims: Not authorship, ownership, permission, endorsement, or creative credit.

terms.definition: The outcomes assigned non-zero probability by a declared finite distribution.
nonclaims: An observed supported outcome does not establish intention or authorship.

terms.definition: The states satisfying a declared finite set of constraints.
nonclaims: Membership does not establish reachability, publication, adoption, or permission.

terms.definition: Existence of a finite directed path from a declared start state under declared transitions.
nonclaims: Reachability does not establish feasibility outside the model, adoption, or authority.

terms.definition: An attributed empirical proposal relating processing dynamics to some reported aesthetic responses under studied conditions.
nonclaims: One model is not a universal law.
It does not convert ease, repetition, symmetry, or familiarity into aesthetic truth.

terms.definition: A declared relation between content, a mode of access, and an explicitly scoped technical criterion.
nonclaims: Not an aesthetic verdict.
Not a universal inclusion or standards-conformance claim.
